provenance.reviewNotes: 2026-11-13 internal review: federated learning moved to a specialisation for Edge & Federated; entry-level AI Infrastructure requires infrastructure-as-code and GPU understanding (CUDA at Foundational), not distributed training code; AI Safety expected at Working; Robotics C++ at Proficient; duplicated requirements removed for Data Scientist (Pandas) and Multimodal (NLP, Embeddings); references added for Speech, Graph and Edge. Still an internal draft, not an external expert review.

levels.Foundational: Understands fundamental concepts and can perform basic tasks.
levels.Working: Can complete practical tasks with guidance.
levels.Proficient: Can independently implement, evaluate and troubleshoot practical work.
levels.Advanced: Can design and optimise complex systems and technically justify decisions.

language.Foundational: Reads and writes short scripts using the core syntax.
language.Working: Writes working programs of moderate size, using the standard library and common packages, with some guidance.
language.Proficient: Independently structures, tests and debugs multi-file projects.
language.Advanced: Designs maintainable codebases, profiles and optimises them, and reviews other people's code.

framework.Foundational: Has followed tutorials or run small examples.
framework.Working: Builds a working project with it by following its documentation.
framework.Proficient: Independently designs, debugs and evaluates non-trivial work with it.
framework.Advanced: Optimises performance, extends it, and justifies design choices with evidence.

concept.Working: Applies them in a guided project.
concept.Proficient: Applies them independently to a new problem and evaluates the result.
concept.Advanced: Designs new approaches and analyses trade-offs rigorously.

capability.Foundational: Has done it once by following an example.
capability.Working: Does it in their own projects, with some guidance.
capability.Proficient: Does it routinely and correctly in independent work.
capability.Advanced: Sets the approach for others and handles edge cases and scale.

tool.Foundational: Has used it in a tutorial.
tool.Working: Uses it in their own projects.
tool.Advanced: Runs it at scale, automates it and optimises it.

platform.Foundational: Has used it in a tutorial.
platform.Working: Uses it in their own projects.
platform.Advanced: Runs it at scale, automates it and optimises it.

evidenceForLevel.Foundational: Any use of the skill in your own described work or in a repository.
evidenceForLevel.Working: Code that uses it in at least one public repository, or your own descriptions of it in two or more projects or jobs (the highest level self-described work can reach).
evidenceForLevel.Proficient: Code that uses it in two or more repositories, or one repository with tests, CI or a documented evaluation, or a platform assessment of 3 stars or more.
evidenceForLevel.Advanced: Code that uses it in three or more repositories plus tests, CI, documented evaluation or work experience, or a platform assessment of 4 stars or more. Topics and descriptions alone never reach Advanced.

tiers.required: Needed for the role. Decides alignment; needs evidence we can check ourselves.
tiers.supporting: Strengthens a candidate. Never holds back alignment; described work counts.
tiers.specialisation: Part of a named specialisation track. Optional; shown when it matches your goals or project.

AI Agents.description: LLM agents that plan, call tools and act over multiple steps.
AI Agents.demonstration: An agent that completes multi-step tasks with tools, with failure cases recorded.

AI Safety.description: Identifying and mitigating harmful model behaviour: red-teaming, robustness, bias.
AI Safety.demonstration: A documented safety evaluation or red-team exercise with findings.

AWS.description: Deploying and operating workloads on AWS.
AWS.demonstration: A project deployed on AWS with its infrastructure described.

Apache Airflow.demonstration: An Airflow DAG that runs a multi-step pipeline.

Audio Signal Processing.description: Representing and processing audio signals (spectrograms, filtering, features).
Audio Signal Processing.demonstration: A project that processes audio into features for a downstream task.

Bash.description: Automating work in the shell: scripts, pipes, processes and environment management.
Bash.demonstration: Shell scripts in a repository that automate setup, data download or training runs.

C++.demonstration: A repository with C++ code you wrote that builds and runs.

CI/CD.description: Automated build, test and deployment pipelines.
CI/CD.demonstration: A repository with a CI pipeline that runs tests on each change.

CUDA.demonstration: A CUDA kernel or GPU optimisation with measured speed-up.

Computer Vision.demonstration: A vision model with evaluation on a held-out image set.

Control Systems.description: Feedback control, state estimation and motion planning for physical systems.
Control Systems.demonstration: A controller (PID or better) for a simulated or real robot, with tuning results and plots of its behaviour.

Convolutional Neural Networks.demonstration: A CNN trained and evaluated on an image task.

Data Preparation.description: Cleaning, transforming and splitting real data; feature engineering without leaking test information.
Data Preparation.demonstration: A documented data pipeline that turns a messy real dataset into a clean training set, with the cleaning decisions explained.

Data Structures and Algorithms.description: Choosing and implementing efficient data structures and algorithms.
Data Structures and Algorithms.demonstration: Solved algorithmic problems on an assessed platform, or efficient algorithmic code.

Data Visualization.description: Choosing and building charts that communicate findings accurately to a specific audience.
Data Visualization.demonstration: An analysis notebook or dashboard whose charts answer stated questions, with captions explaining each finding.

Deep Learning.description: Neural network design, training dynamics and regularisation.
Deep Learning.demonstration: A neural network trained from data with its training curves and evaluation.

levelCriteria.Foundational: Explains neurons, layers, loss functions and gradient descent.
levelCriteria.Working: Trains standard architectures on a dataset with guidance.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Designs, trains and debugs networks independently, including regularisation and tuning.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Develops new architectures or training methods and analyses them rigorously.

Differential Privacy.description: Formal privacy guarantees for data analysis and training.
Differential Privacy.demonstration: A project applying a DP mechanism with its privacy budget stated.

Diffusion Models.description: How diffusion models generate images or other media, and how to condition, fine-tune and evaluate them.
Diffusion Models.demonstration: An image-generation project that conditions or fine-tunes a diffusion model and evaluates the outputs.

Distributed Training.description: Training across multiple devices or machines.
Distributed Training.demonstration: A training run using data/model parallelism, with its configuration.

Docker.demonstration: A repository with a Dockerfile that builds and runs the project with one command.

levelCriteria.Working: Writes a Dockerfile that builds and runs their own project.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Writes multi-stage builds, uses Compose, and debugs container issues independently.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Optimises images for size and security and runs containers in production.

Embeddings.description: Turning text, images or other data into vectors and using similarity for search, clustering or recommendations.
Embeddings.demonstration: A semantic search or clustering project that compares at least two embedding models on example queries.

Experimental Design.description: Framing hypotheses, choosing baselines and ablations, controlling randomness and reporting results reproducibly.
Experimental Design.demonstration: An experiment write-up with a hypothesis, baselines, ablations, several random seeds and code that reproduces the numbers.

FastAPI.demonstration: A FastAPI service with documented endpoints.

Federated Learning.description: Training across decentralised clients without centralising data.
Federated Learning.demonstration: A federated training simulation or deployment with results.

Fine-tuning.description: Adapting a pretrained model to a task with supervised or parameter-efficient training.
Fine-tuning.demonstration: A fine-tuned model with the training setup, data description and before/after evaluation.

Generative AI.demonstration: A project that generates content with a model and evaluates its output.

Git.description: Version control: branching, history and collaboration.
Git.demonstration: Public repositories with a meaningful commit history.

Google Cloud.description: Deploying and operating workloads on Google Cloud.
Google Cloud.demonstration: A project deployed on Google Cloud.

Graph Neural Networks.demonstration: A GNN trained on a graph task with evaluation.

Hugging Face Transformers.description: Using and adapting pretrained models with the Transformers library.
Hugging Face Transformers.demonstration: A project that loads, adapts and evaluates a Hugging Face model.

Image Segmentation.demonstration: A segmentation model evaluated with IoU or similar.

JAX.description: Array programming and model training in JAX.
JAX.demonstration: A repository with a JAX model or numerical method.

Knowledge Graphs.description: Modelling and querying entities and relations.
Knowledge Graphs.demonstration: A knowledge graph built and queried for a task.

Kubernetes.description: Deploying and operating containers on Kubernetes.
Kubernetes.demonstration: Kubernetes manifests or charts that deploy a working service.

LLM Evaluation.description: Measuring LLM quality: test sets, metrics, human and model-graded evaluation.
LLM Evaluation.demonstration: An evaluation suite with defined test cases and reported results for an LLM system.

LangChain.description: Composing LLM pipelines and tools with LangChain.
LangChain.demonstration: A working LangChain application in a public repository.

Large Language Models.description: How large language models behave, and how to use them well: context, sampling, limits, cost and failure modes.
Large Language Models.demonstration: A project that uses an LLM (API or open model) for a defined task and reports how well it works.

levelCriteria.Foundational: Explains tokens, context windows, sampling and hallucination.
levelCriteria.Working: Calls LLM APIs or local models in a project and handles their output.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Designs LLM features independently, managing cost, latency, failure modes and evaluation.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Chooses, adapts and optimises models for a product and justifies the trade-offs.

Linear Algebra.description: Vectors, matrices, decompositions and their use in ML.

Linux.description: Working in Linux environments: shell, processes, permissions.
Linux.demonstration: Scripts or setup work that relies on Linux administration.

LlamaIndex.description: Data frameworks for LLM retrieval with LlamaIndex.
LlamaIndex.demonstration: A LlamaIndex application over real data.

MLflow.description: Tracking experiments and managing model versions with MLflow.
MLflow.demonstration: A project that logs runs and models to MLflow.

Machine Learning.description: Framing problems, training, validating and comparing classical ML models.
Machine Learning.demonstration: An end-to-end ML project with a train/validation/test split, a baseline, at least two models and reported metrics.

levelCriteria.Foundational: Explains supervised and unsupervised learning, overfitting and train/test splits.
levelCriteria.Working: Trains and compares standard models on a prepared dataset with guidance.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Frames a real problem, prepares data, trains, validates and compares models independently.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Designs ML systems end to end and justifies modelling choices with evidence.

Matplotlib.demonstration: An analysis with clear, labelled plots.

Model Deployment.description: Packaging a trained model and serving it reliably: an API, a batch job or an app other people can use.
Model Deployment.demonstration: A trained model served behind an API or app that someone else can call, with setup instructions in the repository.

Model Evaluation.description: Choosing metrics, validation splits and baselines; comparing models and analysing errors honestly.
Model Evaluation.demonstration: A project that compares a baseline with at least one model on a held-out set, reports suitable metrics and discusses where the model fails.

levelCriteria.Foundational: Knows accuracy, precision, recall and why a held-out set matters.
levelCriteria.Working: Uses cross-validation and suitable metrics for a project with guidance.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Chooses metrics for the problem, compares against baselines and analyses errors independently.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Designs evaluation protocols, catches leakage and bias, and ties metrics to real-world impact.

Model Monitoring.demonstration: A deployed model or LLM service with logged metrics or traces and a documented check for drift or quality regressions.

Natural Language Processing.description: Text processing, representation and NLP tasks.
Natural Language Processing.demonstration: An NLP system (classification, extraction, generation) with evaluation.

Neo4j.demonstration: A project storing and querying data in Neo4j.

NetworkX.demonstration: An analysis using NetworkX on real graph data.

NumPy.demonstration: Code that uses NumPy for numerical work.

ONNX.description: Exporting and running models in the ONNX format.
ONNX.demonstration: A model exported to ONNX and run with ONNX Runtime.

Object Detection.description: Locating and classifying objects in images.
Object Detection.demonstration: A detector trained or adapted and evaluated with mAP or similar.

On-device ML.description: Running models within device constraints (memory, latency, power).
On-device ML.demonstration: A model running on a phone, microcontroller or edge board, with measurements.

OpenCV.demonstration: A project using OpenCV for image or video processing.

Pandas.description: Cleaning, reshaping and analysing tabular data with pandas.
Pandas.demonstration: An analysis notebook or script using pandas on a real dataset.

Probability.description: Random variables, distributions and probabilistic reasoning.
Probability.demonstration: Work that models uncertainty explicitly (e.g. a probabilistic model or simulation).

Prompt Engineering.description: Designing, testing and iterating prompts and structured outputs.
Prompt Engineering.demonstration: A project where prompts are versioned and compared on a set of test inputs.

PyTorch.description: Building and training models with PyTorch.
PyTorch.demonstration: A repository with a PyTorch model, its own training loop and an evaluation on held-out data.

levelCriteria.Foundational: Understands tensors, basic operations and how a model is structured.
levelCriteria.Working: Builds and trains a basic model with guidance.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Designs training loops, handles datasets, evaluates models and explains results independently.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Optimises training, debugs performance, manages experiments and applies advanced techniques.

Python.description: Writing, structuring and debugging Python programs.

levelCriteria.Foundational: Writes short scripts with variables, loops, functions and lists.
levelCriteria.Working: Writes programs that use packages, files and classes; follows a style guide.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Structures packages, writes tests, handles errors and debugs independently.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Designs maintainable libraries; profiles and optimises performance.

REST APIs.demonstration: A service or client that exposes or integrates a REST API.

ROS.description: Building robot software with the Robot Operating System.
ROS.demonstration: ROS nodes controlling a robot or simulator.

Recommender Systems.description: Ranking and recommending items to users.
Recommender Systems.demonstration: A recommender evaluated with ranking metrics.

Reinforcement Learning.description: Learning policies from rewards: value methods, policy gradients, exploration.
Reinforcement Learning.demonstration: An agent trained in an environment, with learning curves.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation.description: Grounding LLM answers in retrieved documents: chunking, embedding, retrieval and answer synthesis.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation.demonstration: A RAG system over a real document set, with retrieval quality checked on example questions.

levelCriteria.Working: Builds a basic RAG pipeline over a small document set by following a tutorial.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Builds RAG over real documents and measures retrieval and answer quality independently.

SQL.description: Querying, joining and aggregating relational data.
SQL.demonstration: A project or analysis with non-trivial SQL queries over real data.

Simulation.demonstration: A project that runs experiments in a simulator.

Statistics.demonstration: An analysis that states a hypothesis, applies a suitable test or interval, and interprets the uncertainty in plain words.

levelCriteria.Foundational: Computes and interprets descriptive statistics and distributions.
levelCriteria.Working: Applies common tests and confidence intervals correctly with guidance.
levelCriteria.Proficient: Chooses suitable methods independently and explains uncertainty and assumptions.
levelCriteria.Advanced: Designs studies and handles complex inference such as causal or Bayesian analysis.

TensorFlow.description: Building and training models with TensorFlow/Keras.
TensorFlow.demonstration: A repository with a TensorFlow model and evaluation.

TensorFlow Lite.description: Deploying TensorFlow models to mobile and embedded devices.
TensorFlow Lite.demonstration: A TFLite model running on a device.

TensorRT.demonstration: A model optimised with TensorRT and benchmarked.

Terraform.demonstration: Terraform code that provisions real infrastructure.

Text-to-Speech.demonstration: A TTS pipeline with sample outputs and a quality check.

Time Series Analysis.demonstration: A forecasting project with a time-aware validation split.

Transformers (architecture).demonstration: An implementation or modification of a transformer component, with results.

Triton Inference Server.demonstration: A model deployed on Triton with its configuration.

TypeScript.demonstration: A repository with TypeScript code you wrote.

Vector Databases.description: Storing and querying embeddings for similarity search.
Vector Databases.demonstration: A project that indexes embeddings in a vector store and queries them.

Vision-Language Models.description: Models that jointly process images and text.
Vision-Language Models.demonstration: A project using or adapting a VLM, with evaluation.

Weights & Biases.demonstration: A project logging runs to Weights & Biases.

scikit-learn.demonstration: A repository using scikit-learn pipelines with cross-validation and a held-out evaluation.

spaCy.demonstration: A spaCy pipeline used on real text.

vLLM.demonstration: An LLM served with vLLM, with throughput or latency measured.

ai_product_founder.completionCriteria: Every required competency is at its expected level, shown by independent evidence (repositories, platform activity or assessments).

ml_engineer.label: ML Engineer
ml_engineer.summary: Turns data into trained, evaluated models and ships them inside products.
ml_engineer.distinguishingFocus: Unlike a Data Scientist, the job ends with a model running in software, not a report; unlike an MLOps Engineer, the model itself is the core work.
responsibilities: Frame business problems as ML tasks
Package and deploy models into products
practicalCapabilities: Take a prediction problem from raw data to a deployed model
Choose metrics and baselines that match the business goal
Explain why one model was chosen over another
ml_engineer.projectContext: an end-to-end model you train, evaluate and deploy

specialisations.description: Pipelines, automation and monitoring at scale.

competencies.rationale: Almost all ML engineering code is written in Python.
The core of the job: framing, training and comparing models.
Needed to judge whether a model's improvement is real.
Most model quality comes from how the data is prepared.
Choosing metrics and validation decides which model ships.
The standard toolkit for classical models and pipelines.
The most common framework for neural models in industry and research.
A model only creates value once others can use it.
Training data usually lives in databases.
Keeps ML code correct as it changes.
Explains what models compute and why they fail.
A common way to serve a model behind an API.
Tracks experiments so results can be compared and reproduced.
Version control for code and collaboration.
Many teams train and deploy on a cloud platform.
For images, text and other unstructured data.
The architecture behind most modern models.
Runs training and serving at scale.
Catches drift and regressions after release.
Automates testing and release of models.

ml_engineer.completionCriteria: Every required competency is at its expected level, shown by independent evidence (repositories, platform activity or assessments). Supporting and specialisation competencies never decide it.

data_scientist.label: Data Scientist
data_scientist.summary: Answers questions with data: analysis, experiments and predictive models that inform decisions.
data_scientist.distinguishingFocus: Unlike an ML Engineer, the output is usually an insight, a decision or a prototype model rather than production software.
responsibilities: Design and analyse experiments such as A/B tests
Build predictive models and explain them
practicalCapabilities: Answer a business question with a reproducible analysis
Design an experiment and interpret its result correctly
Present findings clearly with appropriate charts
data_scientist.projectContext: an analysis of a real dataset with a written conclusion

competencies.rationale: The main language for analysis and modelling.
The foundation of every sound conclusion drawn from data.
Most business data has to be queried from databases.
Real data is messy; analysis quality depends on cleaning it well.
Findings only matter if others understand them.
Predictive models are a regular part of the job.
Needed to know whether a model is actually useful.
A/B tests and experiments drive many product decisions.
The usual tool for the data preparation the role requires.
The usual library for building models in analysis work.
Helps understand models such as regression and PCA.
Forecasting demand, sales or metrics over time.
Putting a model where others can use it.

data_scientist.completionCriteria: Every required competency is at its expected level, shown by independent evidence (repositories, platform activity or assessments). Supporting and specialisation competencies never decide it.

deep_learning_engineer.label: Deep Learning Engineer
deep_learning_engineer.summary: Designs, trains and improves neural networks.
deep_learning_engineer.distinguishingFocus: Deeper on neural network training and architecture than an ML Engineer; less on classical models and product integration.
responsibilities: Design and train neural network architectures
Tune, debug and evaluate training runs
Optimise models for speed and memory
practicalCapabilities: Train a network from scratch and diagnose why training fails
Reproduce a published architecture and its results
Make a model faster or smaller without losing accuracy
deep_learning_engineer.projectContext: a neural network you train and evaluate from scratch

competencies.rationale: Deep learning code is written in Python.
Designing, training and debugging neural networks is the daily work: architectures, losses, optimisation and regularisation.
The dominant framework for building and training networks.
Every layer is linear algebra; debugging needs it.
The architecture behind most current models.
Data loading and augmentation shape what a network learns.
Loss functions and generative models are probabilistic.
Ablations show which changes actually help.
Version control for experiments and code.
The standard library for pretrained language models.

deep_learning_engineer.completionCriteria: Every required competency is at its expected level, shown by independent evidence (repositories, platform activity or assessments). Supporting and specialisation competencies never decide it.

generative_ai_engineer.label: Generative AI Engineer
generative_ai_engineer.summary: Builds systems that generate text, images or other content, and makes their output reliable.
generative_ai_engineer.distinguishingFocus: Covers generative models broadly (language and images) and their quality; an LLM Application Engineer focuses on product software around LLMs.
responsibilities: Build generation pipelines over an organisation's data
Ground model output in retrieved knowledge
Evaluate generated content for quality and safety
Adapt models with prompting or fine-tuning
practicalCapabilities: Build a grounded generation pipeline and measure its quality
Choose between prompting, retrieval and fine-tuning for a use case
Explain and reduce hallucinations
generative_ai_engineer.projectContext: a generation pipeline over your own data

competencies.rationale: The language of generative AI tooling.
Most generative systems are built on LLMs.
Knowing the families of generative models and their limits.
The first lever for controlling output.
The basis of retrieval and semantic search.
Grounds output in real data, which most products need.
Generated output must be measured, not assumed correct.
Adapts a model when prompting is not enough.
Needed to work with open models directly.
Generated content can be harmful or misleading.
Models that read and write across modalities.

generative_ai_engineer.completionCriteria: Every required competency is at its expected level, shown by independent evidence (repositories, platform activity or assessments). Supporting and specialisation competencies never decide it.

llm_application_engineer.label: LLM Application Engineer
llm_application_engineer.summary: Builds reliable software products on top of LLMs: APIs, retrieval, tools and user-facing features.
llm_application_engineer.distinguishingFocus: A software engineering role first: integration, reliability, testing and user experience around LLMs, rather than training models.
responsibilities: Connect models to data with retrieval
Test, evaluate and monitor LLM features in production
practicalCapabilities: Ship an LLM feature that handles failures gracefully
Measure whether a prompt or retrieval change made things better
Keep latency and cost within budget

specialisations.description: Features that plan and use tools.

competencies.rationale: The usual backend language for LLM work.
Using models well: context, cost and failure modes.
The main way to shape model behaviour in an app.
Most LLM apps need answers grounded in real data.
LLM features are delivered and integrated through APIs.
Without evaluation, changes can silently make things worse.
A common orchestration framework (one option among several).
A common way to build the API layer in Python.
Many LLM products have a TypeScript front end or backend.
Apps store users and data in databases.
Prompt injection and data leakage are real product risks.
A popular framework for AI web products.
Features that plan and call tools.
Tracing quality, latency and cost in production.

llm_application_engineer.completionCriteria: Every required competency is at its expected level, shown by independent evidence (repositories, platform activity or assessments). Supporting and specialisation competencies never decide it.

llm_model_engineer.label: LLM Model Engineer
llm_model_engineer.summary: Trains, fine-tunes, evaluates and optimises language models themselves.
llm_model_engineer.distinguishingFocus: Works on the model weights, unlike an LLM Application Engineer who builds products on top of existing models.
responsibilities: Fine-tune and adapt open language models
practicalCapabilities: Fine-tune an open model and show it improved on a held-out benchmark
Explain a transformer's internals and training dynamics
Trade off quality, speed and memory deliberately
llm_model_engineer.projectContext: fine-tuning and evaluating an open language model

competencies.rationale: Language models are deep networks; training them needs this.
